sender.en: A friendly stranger on WhatsApp or Instagram who says they work with investment brokers, then a Telegram group

name.en: Task or trading group: small early profits, then “pay to unfreeze your account”

how.en: A stranger messages you on WhatsApp or social media with a way to earn extra income: tasks or trading on a “secure platform” paying a set amount each day. You are added to a Telegram group, given small early profits and encouraged to deposit more. When you try to withdraw, you are told there is a technical error or a frozen account and must pay again. The UAE Ministry of Interior shared the case of a man who lost Dh42,000 this way; other residents lost AED85,711, AED200,000 and AED70,000.

text.en: A stranger offers extra income through tasks or trading.
You are moved to a Telegram group or a trading app.
Small early profits, then bigger deposits to personal accounts.
To withdraw, you must first pay a “fee” to unfreeze the account.

Hello dear, I work with an investment broker team. We have a simple online task: you can earn AED 100 to AED 325 every day without leaving your job. Many members in UAE are already withdrawing profits. Shall I add you to our Telegram group?

en: added to a telegram group to earn money doing tasks
they asked me to pay to unfreeze my account before withdrawing
made small profits then deposited more
woman on whatsapp said she works with investment brokers
could not withdraw my balance from the trading platform
Fixed daily profits for simple tasks or trading.
Deposits to personal accounts or crypto wallets.
A fee to release money that is already “yours”.
Stop paying, even to “unfreeze” a balance.
Check whether the platform is licensed by the Securities and Commodities Authority before investing.
Report it to your bank and the police straight away.

sources.title: UAE experts warn against unlicensed trading platforms promising quick wealth
Dh42,000 lost in scam: UAE Ministry of Interior warns against fake trading platforms
Fake investments, travel deals: UAE warn against social media scams

story.en: A man received a social media message offering extra income from a “secure trading platform” paying Dh100 to Dh325 a day. After small early gains he kept investing until his virtual balance reached Dh42,000. When he tried to withdraw, he was told there was a technical error and paid another Dh42,000 to “unfreeze” the account before realising it was a scam.
